name: Margaret Wilson
chief_complaint: Sudden onset right-sided weakness and slurred speech - started 90 minutes ago
opening_statement: My husband called the ambulance because I suddenly couldn't move my right arm and leg properly. My speech is slurred and I'm having trouble finding words. It happened suddenly while I was having breakfast this morning at 8:30am.
emotional_baseline: Anxious, frustrated by communication difficulty, cooperative with examination

symptoms.symptom: Right hemiparesis (weakness of right arm and leg)

socrates.onset: Sudden onset at 08:30 (90 minutes ago) - witnessed by husband
socrates.character: Unable to lift right arm against gravity, dragging right leg when walking
socrates.radiation: Affects entire right side (face, arm, leg)
socrates.timing: Constant since onset, no improvement or fluctuation
socrates.severity: Moderate - MRC power 3/5 right arm, 4/5 right leg

rag_citation.source: eTG Neurology 5.1.1: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Clinical Features
rag_citation.quote: Hemiparesis (unilateral weakness) is the most common presentation of anterior circulation stroke - sudden onset distinguishes stroke from TIA

socrates.character: Slurred, difficult to articulate words clearly
socrates.severity: Moderate - speech comprehensible but clearly abnormal

rag_citation.quote: Dysarthria (slurred speech with intact language comprehension) indicates motor pathway involvement - distinguish from dysphasia (language deficit)

symptoms.symptom: Right facial droop (right lower facial weakness)

rag_citation.quote: Lower facial weakness (sparing forehead) indicates contralateral upper motor neuron lesion - typical of stroke (vs Bell's palsy which affects entire hemiface)

symptoms.symptom: Sudden onset (stroke onset time critical for thrombolysis window)

rag_citation.source: eTG Neurology 5.1.2: Acute Stroke Management - Time Windows
rag_citation.quote: Thrombolysis window: IV alteplase within 4.5 hours of symptom onset - earlier treatment = better outcomes ('time is brain')

past_medical_history: Atrial fibrillation (diagnosed 2 years ago, rate-controlled, NOT anticoagulated - patient declined warfarin)
Previous TIA (6 months ago - transient right arm weakness, resolved within 1 hour, no imaging performed)
medications: Metoprolol 50mg BD (beta-blocker for AF rate control + hypertension)
Amlodipine 10mg daily (calcium channel blocker for hypertension)
Aspirin 100mg daily (antiplatelet - inadequate for AF stroke prevention)
family_history: Mother had stroke aged 75. Father died from myocardial infarction aged 70.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband, independent with ADLs (prior to stroke)

vitals.bp: 168/94 mmHg (elevated - permissive hypertension in acute stroke, do NOT lower acutely unless >220/120)
vitals.gcs: 14 (E4 V4 M6 - mild expressive difficulty from dysarthria)

neurological.cranial_nerves: Right lower facial weakness (UMN pattern - forehead spared), pupils equal and reactive, extraocular movements intact
neurological.motor: Right arm MRC 3/5 (can move against gravity but not resistance), Right leg MRC 4/5 (can resist some resistance), Left side 5/5 (normal)
neurological.sensory: Reduced sensation to light touch on right side (arm and leg)
neurological.reflexes: Brisk right-sided reflexes (biceps, triceps, knee, ankle), upgoing right plantar (Babinski sign - UMN lesion)
neurological.coordination: Unable to perform finger-nose test on right due to weakness, left side normal
neurological.gait: Unable to walk safely (right leg weakness, fall risk)

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular pulse (AF), no murmurs, no carotid bruits, JVP not elevated

investigations.ct_brain_non_contrast: URGENT - no hemorrhage, no early ischemic changes visible, no mass lesion (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score 10/10)
investigations.ct_angiography: Left MCA occlusion (proximal M1 segment) - candidate for thrombectomy if within 6-hour window
investigations.ecg: Atrial fibrillation with ventricular rate 92 bpm, no acute ischemic changes
investigations.fbc: Hemoglobin 136 g/L, WCC 8.2 x10⁹/L, Platelets 245 x10⁹/L (normal coagulation profile)
investigations.ue: Normal renal function (eGFR 68 mL/min), Creatinine 88 μmol/L
investigations.lipids: Total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L, LDL 3.1 mmol/L, HDL 1.3 mmol/L

expected_diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke - left MCA territory (cardioembolic from atrial fibrillation - inadequate anticoagulation)
expected_management: TIME-CRITICAL MANAGEMENT (CODE STROKE ACTIVATION):
1. Door-to-needle time <60 minutes (currently 90 minutes from symptom onset - WITHIN 4.5-HOUR WINDOW)
2. CT brain non-contrast (URGENT) - EXCLUDE hemorrhage before thrombolysis
3. CT angiography (if available) - identify large vessel occlusion (thrombectomy candidate)
THROMBOLYSIS (IF NO CONTRAINDICATIONS):
4. IV alteplase (tPA) 0.9mg/kg (max 90mg):
- 10% as bolus over 1 minute
- 90% as infusion over 60 minutes
- Contraindications: hemorrhage on CT, INR >1.7, platelets <100, BP >185/110 (treat first), recent surgery/trauma
5. Monitor BP during thrombolysis: target <185/110 mmHg (use labetalol 10mg IV if needed)
6. Neurological observations q15min during infusion, then q30min × 6h, then q1h × 24h
MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY (IF LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION):
7. Transfer to interventional neuroradiology if:
- Large vessel occlusion (MCA, ICA) on CTA
- NIHSS ≥6
- Within 6-hour window (up to 24h if penumbra on imaging)
- ASPECTS ≥6 (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score)
SUPPORTIVE MANAGEMENT:
8. Aspirin 300mg (give 24 hours AFTER thrombolysis, or immediately if thrombolysis not given)
9. Permissive hypertension (allow BP up to 220/120) - do NOT lower acutely unless >220/120 or aortic dissection
10. IV fluids 0.9% NaCl to maintain euvolemia (avoid hypotonic fluids - worsen cerebral edema)
11. Normoglycemia target 4-11 mmol/L (avoid hypoglycemia <4 mmol/L)
12. Normothermia (paracetamol if fever - fever worsens stroke outcomes)
13. Dysphagia screen (before oral intake) - risk of aspiration pneumonia
14. VTE prophylaxis: compression stockings (avoid heparin for 24h post-thrombolysis)
SECONDARY PREVENTION (POST-ACUTE PHASE):
15. Anticoagulation for AF - START WITHIN 14 DAYS:
- DOAC preferred (apixaban 5mg BD, rivaroxaban 20mg daily, dabigatran 150mg BD)
- Warfarin alternative (target INR 2-3)
- Timing: 1-3-6-12 day rule (TIA = 1 day, minor stroke = 3 days, moderate = 6 days, severe = 12 days)
16. High-intensity statin: atorvastatin 80mg nocte (regardless of baseline lipids)
17. Optimize BP control: target <130/80 mmHg after acute phase (ACE inhibitor + thiazide)
18. Optimize diabetes control: HbA1c <7%
REHABILITATION:
19. Early mobilization (within 24-48h if stable)
20. Multidisciplinary stroke team: physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy
21. Stroke unit admission (reduces mortality by 20%)
MONITORING:
22. Monitor for hemorrhagic transformation (post-thrombolysis ICH risk 6-7%)
23. Repeat CT brain if neurological deterioration or pre-discharge
24. Echocardiogram (detect cardioembolic source - thrombus, valve disease)

critical_errors.error: Delayed thrombolysis beyond 4.5-hour window (door-to-needle time >60 minutes)
critical_errors.explanation: Every 15-minute delay reduces likelihood of good outcome by 4% - 'time is brain' (1.9 million neurons lost per minute)

critical_errors.error: Aggressive BP lowering in acute stroke (target <140/90) causing hypoperfusion of ischemic penumbra
critical_errors.explanation: Permissive hypertension required to maintain cerebral perfusion - only treat if BP >220/120 mmHg

critical_errors.error: Failed to give aspirin 300mg within 24 hours (in patient who did not receive thrombolysis)
critical_errors.explanation: Aspirin 300mg within 48h reduces early stroke recurrence by 30% - delayed beyond 48h loses benefit

critical_errors.error: Started anticoagulation immediately (day 0) in moderate stroke instead of day 6 (1-3-6-12 rule)
critical_errors.explanation: Early anticoagulation increases hemorrhagic transformation risk - use 1-3-6-12 day rule based on stroke severity

critical_errors.error: Failed to exclude stroke mimics (hypoglycemia, seizure, Todd's paresis) before thrombolysis
critical_errors.explanation: Hypoglycemia can mimic stroke - MUST check glucose before thrombolysis (avoid thrombolyzing non-stroke)

critical_errors.error: Continued aspirin as sole antiplatelet in patient with AF (inadequate stroke prevention)
critical_errors.explanation: AF requires anticoagulation (DOAC or warfarin) - aspirin provides only 20% risk reduction vs 65% with anticoagulation

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRACP, Neurologist, 19 years post-fellowship, Stroke specialist
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent - classic MCA stroke presentation with cardioembolic source (AF not anticoagulated)
fracp_reviews.difficulty_appropriate: Yes - Medium difficulty appropriate (time-critical thrombolysis decision, AF management)
fracp_reviews.rag_citations_correct: Yes - eTG 5.1 citations verified and accurate
fracp_reviews.feedback: Excellent neurology persona. Critical emphasis on time windows (4.5h thrombolysis, 6h thrombectomy). Good inclusion of permissive hypertension concept (common error to lower BP acutely). Consider adding NIHSS score calculation teaching points for completeness. 1-3-6-12 day rule for anticoagulation timing correctly identified.

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRACP, General Physician with stroke experience, 14 years post-fellowship
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate acute stroke management - appropriate thrombolysis pathway and secondary prevention
fracp_reviews.feedback: Good persona. Management pathway correct (thrombolysis → aspirin 24h later → DOAC day 6). Excellent inclusion of AF as cardioembolic source (patient on aspirin only - inadequate). Suggest adding brief mention of carotid imaging (carotid stenosis screening) for secondary prevention completeness.

learning_objectives: Recognize acute ischemic stroke presentation (sudden onset hemiparesis, dysarthria, facial droop)
Apply Code Stroke protocol (door-to-needle <60 minutes for thrombolysis)
Understand thrombolysis window (IV alteplase within 4.5 hours of symptom onset)
Apply permissive hypertension in acute stroke (allow BP up to 220/120 mmHg)
Initiate anticoagulation for AF-related stroke using 1-3-6-12 day rule (moderate stroke = day 6)
Recognize cardioembolic stroke risk in AF (aspirin inadequate - requires anticoagulation)
Exclude stroke mimics before thrombolysis (hypoglycemia, seizure)
